page: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-amd is an entry-tier virtual server instance from the High Performance family, configured with 2 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The execution topology allocates two hardware threads across a single physical core, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is provisioned at 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding a ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled directly with 100 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address. The configuration does not include discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate moderate single-threaded capability coupled with restrained multi-core execution. The processor recorded a stress-ng single-core score of 2263.16, falling within the middle 50% percentile, while the multi-core stress-ng result of 4483.12 remained in the lower quartile. Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 1116.0 and a multi-core score of 2013.0, alongside lower-range ratings for software compilation and data parsing. System memory sustained large-block uncached read speeds of 20.06 GB/sec and write speeds of 20.37 GB/sec, corresponding to a Redis SET benchmark rate of 1.85 million operations per second and static web throughput of 1.3 GB/sec.

Operating on shared CPU threads means computational throughput is susceptible to multi-tenant contention during sustained execution cycles. However, the presence of integrated NVMe storage paired with modest memory density provides efficient baseline execution for bounded tasks. The instance is suited for staging environments, development servers, lightweight web endpoints, small microservices, and asynchronous task workers that do not mandate sustained multi-core processing.
